title: Mulligatawny Soup
subtitle: An Anglo-Indian spiced broth
excerpt: A thick, gently spiced soup of chicken, lentils, and apple with coconut milk. It is warming and substantial, with a mellow curry flavour. Serve with rice or crusty bread.

recipe.sourceNotes: Mulligatawny (from the Tamil 'milagu tanni', meaning pepper water) entered British cookery during the colonial period in India and became a fixture of Anglo-Indian and Victorian British cooking. Many British recipe books from the nineteenth century onward include a version.

content.text: Mulligatawny is a thick, spiced soup made with chicken, red lentils, apple, and coconut milk. The apple gives it a faint sweetness that softens the spices, and the lentils make it filling enough to be a meal on its own. It is one of the soups that improves a day in the fridge.
Melt the butter in a large saucepan over a medium heat. Add the onion, carrot, and celery. Cook for 8 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in the curry powder and ground cinnamon. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Add the apple and lentils and stir to coat in the spices.
Pour in the stock and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for 25 minutes until the lentils have completely softened and the vegetables are tender.
Use a stick blender to partially blend the soup in the pot, leaving some texture. Alternatively, blend half and stir it back.
Stir in the coconut milk and shredded chicken. Simmer gently for 5 minutes. Add the lemon juice and salt. Taste and adjust seasoning before serving.
